rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4-5 and Tables 1-6 report the authors' own proof-of-concept implementation (YF-201 flow sensor, LoRaWAN, Ethereum Ropsten) and bench measurements of program size, memory, processing time, transaction cost/latency and energy consumption on six microcontroller boards.
rows.notes: The study's own results are purely technical benchmarks: device footprints, processing times, 45% payload compression, Ethereum transaction costs and ~32 s average confirmation, and ~6% additional energy for blockchain operations. Trust, data security and facilitated water sharing among farmers are asserted as design properties of the architecture (Section 3), not measured; no farmers, stakeholders or water-sharing outcomes were studied. The study shows only the technical precondition (constrained metering devices can act as signed, direct data sources on a public blockchain), so the claimed social effect is upstream of what was tested. Security analysis is explicitly listed as future work.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4-5 and Tables 1-6 report the authors' own proof-of-concept implementation and bench measurements of memory, time, transaction cost and energy on six IoT boards.
rows.notes: No water use, water savings or water-use-efficiency outcome was measured. The incentive/rewarding smart contract (Reward() relative to a threshold) is implemented and its gas cost reported, but its effect on farmers' water consumption was never evaluated; the irrigation schedule used in the energy budget (2 h twice daily) is an assumption, not an observation. The study only establishes the technical feasibility of metering devices feeding a blockchain-based incentive system, a precondition of the claimed water-efficiency effect.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is an engineering proof-of-concept evaluating device-level feasibility (energy, memory, time, cost) of constrained flow-metering IoT devices as direct blockchain actors; it contains no evidence on social or water-use outcomes, which it only motivates conceptually.
